title: Finishing the build
say: LittleBot, version five. Finishing the build. First the battery plug, then the deck and all its wires, a test, and then the body, the cap, the head and the arms. In an order that leaves room for your hands and your screwdriver at every step. Pause whenever you need.

title: Where you are
done: Wheels, motors and casters in the base
Pi + UPS, under the stack keeper
Drive switch in the tub's front wall
Speaker, mic and arm servos in the body
Neck and head servo on the cap
RP2040: its program, on the breadboard
Batteries in their holder, in the drawer
say: Here's where you are. Done: the wheels, motors and casters, the Pi and its UPS, the drive switch, the speaker, the mic and the arm servos in the body, the head with its screen and camera, and the neck with the head servo. The R P twenty forty has its program, and sits on its breadboard. Still to do, in this order: the battery plug and the fuse, the switch, the deck and every wire on it, a test, and then the body, the cap, the head and the arms. The batteries go in last.

title: Why this order
head: Why this order
items: Its tabs end up under the deck: wire them while the deck is off.
The motor driver goes on with the deck
2 of its corner screws are also the deck's screws.
Every Pi wire before the body
Once the body is on, you can't reach the Pi or the deck.
A loose wire is a 1-minute fix now, a big job later.
The head's alignment before the cap
The head servo's gears are under the cap.
say: Why this order? The switch's tabs end up under the deck, so they're wired first. Two of the motor driver's corner screws are also the deck's screws, so the driver goes on with the deck. Every wire to the Pi goes in before the body covers it. Everything is tested while you can still reach it. And the head's direction is checked before the cap hides the head servo's gears.

title: What you need
items: plug in the batteries: not yet
say: You'll need: a soldering iron and solder, the heat shrink that came with your X T thirty plugs, a wire stripper, a small flat screwdriver, a multimeter, jumper wires, male to male and male to female, some zip ties, and tape and a pen, for labels. For the short power wires, use your spare X T thirty pairs: cut the plug off, and you have red and black wire. And don't plug in the batteries until the video says so.

part: Part 1 · The battery plug and fuse (at the bench)
title: The batteries' path
cap: batteries → plug → 5 A fuse → switch → Wago A (+)
the plug's black → Wago B (−)
say: Part one. The batteries' path. From the batteries, through a plug, through the five amp fuse, through the switch, to Wago A. The black side goes straight to Wago B. The fuse is there so that a short circuit blows a cheap fuse, instead of melting a wire.

part: Part 1 · The battery plug and fuse (at the bench)
title: How to join two wires
cap: 1 heat-shrink on · 2 strip 8 mm · 3 twist
4 solder · 5 slide the heat-shrink over · 6 shrink it
say: First, how to join two wires. Slide a piece of heat shrink onto one wire. Strip about eight millimetres from both ends. Twist the bare ends together. Hold the iron under the twist, and feed solder onto the top, until it flows into the strands. Let it cool, slide the heat shrink over the joint, and shrink it with a hair dryer on hot, or the side of the iron, kept moving.

part: Part 1 · The battery plug and fuse (at the bench)
title: The batteries' half of the plug
cap: The FEMALE half (holes) goes on the battery holder
red to red, black to black: solder + heat-shrink each
The male half (pins) stays in the robot
say: Take one X T thirty pair. The female half, the one with holes, goes on the battery holder. Join red to red, and black to black, each one soldered and covered with heat shrink. The male half, with the pins, stays in the robot. The plug only fits one way round, so plus always meets plus.

part: Part 1 · The battery plug and fuse (at the bench)
title: The fuse holder
cap: Cut its wire loop in the middle: 2 leads
Strip both ends
Its fuse out, a tan 5 A fuse in, cap closed
say: The fuse holder. Cut its wire loop in the middle. Now it has two leads. Strip both ends. Pull out the fuse it came with, push in a five amp fuse, the tan one, and close the cap. Keep a spare five amp fuse somewhere safe.

part: Part 1 · The battery plug and fuse (at the bench)
title: The robot's half: red to the fuse
note: its black stays free: it goes straight to Wago B
cap: The male XT30's red → one fuse lead: solder + heat-shrink
Leave its black wire free for now
say: Now the robot's half: the male X T thirty, the one with pins. Join its red wire to one of the fuse holder's leads, the same way. Leave its black wire free for now. It will go straight into Wago B.

part: Part 2 · The switch (the deck still off)
title: Which two tabs?
cap: Meter on beep
The 2 tabs that beep with the switch ON, not OFF
The 3rd tab only lights it: leave it empty
say: Part two, the switch, while the deck is still off. Once the deck is on, its tabs are underneath it. The switch has three tabs. Set your meter to beep. Find the two tabs that beep when the switch is on, and stay silent when it's off. Use those two. The third tab only lights the switch. Leave it empty.

part: Part 2 · The switch (the deck still off)
title: The fuse's other lead onto a tab
tip: keep the hot iron off the plastic tub
cap: Through the tab's hole, bend it over, solder it
Then heat-shrink or tape over the tab
say: Solder the fuse holder's free lead to one of those two tabs. Poke the bare end through the tab's hole, bend it over, and solder it. Keep the hot iron away from the plastic. Then cover the tab with heat shrink, or wrap it in tape.

part: Part 2 · The switch (the deck still off)
title: A red wire on the other tab
lab: a red wire, about 20 cm: to Wago A
cap: About 20 cm of red wire (a spare XT30 red)
Its other end goes to Wago A, later
say: On the other tab, solder a red wire, about twenty centimetres long. A spare X T thirty red works. Its other end will go to Wago A. Now the plug and the fuse hang into the drawer's bay. Two loose ends wait to go up through the deck: this red wire, and the plug's black.

part: Part 2 · The switch (the deck still off)
title: Under the deck: check before it goes on
cap: The switch's 2 wires done; the plug hangs in the bay
Each motor's tail zip-tied in its saddle
Each motor's 6 wires up at the back, beside the Pi
say: Before the deck goes on, look underneath one last time. The switch is wired. Each motor's tail is zip tied into its saddle. And each motor's six wires run up at the back, beside the Pi's mount. That's where they come up past the deck.

part: Part 3 · The boards onto the deck (at the bench)
title: Where everything sits on the deck
cap: The robot's front is at the bottom
breadboard: robot's left · motor driver: right · Wagos: middle
say: Part three, the boards onto the deck, at the bench. Here's the deck from above, with the robot's front at the bottom. The breadboard goes on the robot's left. The motor driver on its right, with the converter in front of it. The four Wagos sit in a block in the middle. And the notch at the front edge is where the battery wires come up.

part: Part 3 · The boards onto the deck (at the bench)
title: The breadboard: its sticky back
pins: GP0 side: towards the back (the Pi)
a screw hole under it: leave it empty
cap: USB end to the middle, the GP0 side to the back
Peel the paper off its back, press it into the 4 corner guides
No sticky pad? Double-sided tape or hot glue
say: The breadboard. Turn it so the R P twenty forty's U S B end points to the middle of the robot, and the G P zero side, where the Pi's wires go, faces the back. There's a screw hole under it: it stays empty. Peel the paper off the breadboard's sticky back, and press it down between its four corner guides. If yours has no sticky pad, use double sided tape, or a few dabs of hot glue.

part: Part 3 · The boards onto the deck (at the bench)
title: The motor driver: 2 screws for now
cap: Its screw terminals face the back
2 × M3 × 8 in its 2 OUTER corners only
Its 2 inner holes sit over the tub's posts: long screws, later
say: The motor driver. Its screw terminals face the back. Look at its four corner holes. The two nearest the middle sit right over two of the tub's posts, so they get long screws later, through the deck. For now, fit only the two outer corners: two M three by eight, into the deck's short posts.

part: Part 3 · The boards onto the deck (at the bench)
title: The Wagos: A, B, C, D
cap: Label them with tape: A, B, C, D
A, B on the right, levers to the driver; C, D on the left
A and C at the front · zip tie them once their wires are in
say: The Wagos. Label them with tape: A, B, C and D. A and B go on the right, their levers facing the motor driver. C and D on the left, their levers facing the breadboard. A and C at the front. Don't zip tie them yet. That's easier once their wires are in.

part: Part 3 · The boards onto the deck (at the bench)
title: The converter
cap: Into its little fence at the front right
A zip tie through its 2 slots
Read its labels: which wires are IN, which are OUT
say: The converter goes into its little fence, at the front right. Hold it down with a zip tie, through the two slots. Read the labels on it: which wires are in, and which are out.

part: Part 4 · The deck onto the tub
title: Lower it, 3 screws
cap: The switch's red + the plug's black up through the front notch
2 × M3 × 16 through the driver's inner corners into the posts
1 × M3 × 8 at the back left · front left: under the breadboard, empty
say: Part four. Pull the switch's red wire and the plug's black wire up through the notch at the front of the deck. Lower the deck onto its posts. Two M three by sixteen go down through the motor driver's inner corners, through the deck, and into the tub's posts. One M three by eight goes into the post at the back left, just behind the breadboard. The front left post is under the breadboard. It stays empty.

part: Part 4 · The deck onto the tub
title: The wires that come up
cap: Each motor: red + white → the driver; 4 thin wires → the breadboard
The switch's red → Wago A · the plug's black → Wago B
Next: the drawing, wire by wire
say: Now the wires come up. Each motor's red and white go to the motor driver, and its four thin wires to the breadboard. The switch's red goes to Wago A, and the plug's black to Wago B. From here on, the drawing shows each wire, one at a time.

title: How a Wago works
cap: Strip 11 mm · lever up · wire in all the way · lever down · tug
All 5 slots of a Wago are joined: only the letter matters
Thin jumper wire: strip 22 mm, fold it in half, twist it
say: Part five, power. How a Wago works. Strip eleven millimetres. Lift the orange lever, push the wire in all the way, and close the lever. Then tug it. It must not come out. All five slots of one Wago are joined inside, so any slot will do. Only the letter matters. Jumper wire is thin: strip twice as much, fold the bare end in half, and twist it, so the lever can grip it.

title: Everything, laid out flat
cap: The RP2040 is drawn chip side down, like yours:
GP0 to GP15 on the right · Vin, 3V3, GP26, GP16 on the left
Breadboard letters as printed: a-e left, f-j right
say: Here's everything, laid out flat. The R P twenty forty is drawn chip side down, the way yours sits, so G P zero to fifteen are on the right. The letters on the breadboard are the ones printed on yours: a to e on the left, f to j on the right.

title: The switch and the plug
cap: The switch's red wire → Wago A
The plug's black wire → Wago B
say: The switch's red wire goes into Wago A. The plug's black wire goes into Wago B.

title: The motors' red and white
cap: Left motor: red → M1A, white → M1B
Right motor: red → M2A, white → M2B
Ends in a socket? Cut it off, strip 6 mm, into the terminal
say: The motors. Loosen the screw terminals on the motor driver. Left motor: red to M one A, white to M one B. Right motor: red to M two A, white to M two B. If the wires end in little sockets, cut them off, and strip six millimetres. Push each bare end in, and tighten.

title: The motor driver's power
cap: Its green block: + → Wago A · − → Wago B
Use a spare XT30's red and black
say: The motor driver's green power block. Plus goes to Wago A, and minus to Wago B. A spare X T thirty's red and black are just right for this.

title: The converter's input
cap: IN + → Wago A · IN − → Wago B
say: The converter turns the batteries into five volts, for the servos and the R P twenty forty. Its input: plus to Wago A, minus to Wago B.

title: The converter's output
cap: OUT + → Wago C · OUT − → Wago D
If its output ends in a plug: cut it off, strip the 2 wires
say: Its output: plus to Wago C, minus to Wago D. If the output ends in a plug, cut the plug off, and strip the two wires.

title: Link the two grounds
cap: A short black wire: Wago B → Wago D
say: Then link the two ground Wagos, with a short black wire from Wago B to Wago D.

title: Check for shorts (no batteries)
cap: Switch OFF, meter on beep
A to B: no beep · C to D: no beep
A chirp that stops at once is the capacitors: fine
say: Now check for shorts, with no batteries. Switch off, and set the meter to beep. Touch Wago A and Wago B: it must not beep. Then Wago C and Wago D: no beep. A short chirp that stops at once is just the capacitors charging. That's fine.

title: A quick live test
cap: Drawer in front of the robot, its plug into the one in the bay
Switch ON: A to B 7 to 9.5 V · C to D 5 V
Switch OFF and unplug again
say: A quick live test. Set the drawer in front of the robot, and push its plug into the plug in the bay. Switch on. The switch lights up. Red probe on Wago A, black on Wago B: seven to nine and a half volts. Red on Wago C, black on Wago D: five volts. If either is wrong, switch off and check. Then switch off, and unplug.

title: Its power
cap: Vin (row 2, left) → Wago C
GND (row 3, left) → Wago B
Cut a jumper, strip and fold its cut end for the Wago
say: Part six, the R P twenty forty's wires. Only now, with the five volts checked. First its power. From V in, row two on the left, to Wago C. From the ground pin, row three on the left, to Wago B. For each Wago end, cut a jumper, then strip and fold the cut end.

title: The motor driver's control pins
cap: GP10 → M1A · GP11 → M1B · GP12 → M2A · GP13 → M2B (rows 14-17, right)
GND (row 18, right) → the driver's GND
Male-female jumpers · leave the driver's 5V pin empty
say: The motor driver's control pins, with male to female jumpers. G P ten to M one A. G P eleven to M one B. G P twelve to M two A. G P thirteen to M two B. They're rows fourteen to seventeen, on the right. And the ground in row eighteen, on the right, to the driver's ground. Leave the driver's five volt pin empty.

title: Left motor's encoder
cap: yellow → GP6 (row 9) · green → GP7 (row 10) · black → GND (row 8)
All on the right side
Wires end in sockets? A male-male jumper into each
say: The encoders: each motor's four thin wires. Left motor: yellow to G P six, row nine. Green to G P seven, row ten. Black to the ground in row eight. All on the right side. If the wires end in little sockets, push a male to male jumper into each, and put its other end in the breadboard.

title: Right motor's encoder
cap: yellow → GP8 (row 11) · green → GP9 (row 12) · black → GND (row 13)
say: Right motor: yellow to G P eight, row eleven. Green to G P nine, row twelve. Black to the ground in row thirteen.

title: Both blue wires: 3.3 V
cap: Both blues → 3V3 (row 5, LEFT side)
Never 5 V: the RP2040's pins take 3.3 V only
say: Both blue wires go to three point three volts: row five, on the left side. Never five volts. The R P twenty forty's pins only take three point three.

title: The battery sense: 2 resistors
cap: 22 kΩ (red red orange): b10 → b22
10 kΩ (brown black orange): a10 → a8
say: Two resistors let it measure the batteries. The twenty two k one, with red, red and orange stripes, goes from b ten down to b twenty two. The ten k one, brown, black and orange, goes from a ten up to a eight.

title: Battery + to row 22
cap: Wago A → a22
8.5 V becomes 2.7 V on GP26: safe for the pin
say: Then a wire from Wago A to a twenty two. The resistors turn the batteries' eight and a half volts into under three volts, which the pin can safely read.

title: Three wires each
cap: brown = ground · red = 5 V · orange = signal
The servos are in the body and the cap:
each gets a 'tail' on the deck, to plug onto later
say: Part seven, the servos. Each servo has three wires. Brown is ground, red is power, orange is the signal. The servos are already in the body and on the cap, so each one gets a tail on the deck, ready to plug onto later.

title: Making a long tail
cap: Per wire: a male-male jumper + a male-female on its end
red, brown: cut the free end, strip + fold, into the Wagos
Tape over the joints · label each tail
say: A long tail. For each of the three wires, take a male to male jumper, and push a male to female jumper onto its end. That makes it long enough to reach up into the body. The orange's free end goes into the breadboard. For the red and the brown, cut the free end off, strip and fold it, for the Wagos. Tape over the joints in the middle, so they can't pull apart, and label each tail.

title: The head servo's tail
cap: orange → GP14 (row 19, right)
red → Wago C · brown → Wago D
Label it: HEAD
say: The head servo's tail. Orange to G P fourteen, row nineteen on the right. Red to Wago C. Brown to Wago D. Label it: head.

title: The left arm's tail
cap: orange → GP15 (row 20, right)
red → Wago C · brown → Wago D
say: The left arm's tail. Orange to G P fifteen, row twenty on the right. Red to Wago C. Brown to Wago D.

title: The right arm's tail
cap: orange → GP16 (row 20, LEFT)
red → Wago C · brown → Wago D
say: The right arm's tail. Orange to G P sixteen. That's row twenty, on the left side. Red to Wago C. Brown to Wago D.

part: Part 8 · The link to the Pi
title: The Pi's pins
cap: The 40-pin header, along the Pi's bottom edge
Outer row, counting from the end away from the USB ports:
pins 2, 4 = 5 V (never!) · 6 = GND · 8 = TX · 10 = RX
say: Part eight, the link to the Pi. Its forty pin header runs along its bottom edge. On the outer row, counting from the end away from the U S B ports: pins two and four are five volts. Never touch them. Pin six is ground, pin eight is T X, and pin ten is R X.

part: Part 8 · The link to the Pi
title: Three wires to the Pi
cap: Male-female jumpers, female end on the Pi
GP0 (row 1) → pin 10 · GP1 (row 2) → pin 8: they cross
GND (row 8, right) → pin 6
say: Use male to female jumpers, the female end on the Pi. G P zero, row one, goes to pin ten. G P one, row two, goes to pin eight. They cross over: what one board sends, the other receives. And the ground in row eight, on the right, goes to pin six.

part: Part 8 · The link to the Pi
title: Tidy up
cap: One zip tie over the Wagos, through the 2 slots
Bundle the wires, a little slack before each end
A strip of tape over the jumpers on the Pi and the driver
say: Tidy up. One zip tie goes over the Wagos, through the two slots beside them. Bundle the wires with zip ties, leaving a little slack before each end. And put a strip of tape over the jumpers on the Pi's pins and the motor driver's pins, so they can't slide off.

part: Part 9 · Test it now, while you can reach everything
title: On the Pi, once
cap: Use SSH from your computer,
or plug in the head's screen and a keyboard for now
say: Part nine. Test it now, while you can still reach everything. On the Pi, over S S H, or with the head's screen and a keyboard plugged in for now: if you haven't already, add the line, D T param equals uart zero equals on, at the end of the file, slash boot, slash firmware, slash config dot T X T. Reboot, and get LittleBot's latest code.

part: Part 9 · Test it now, while you can reach everything
title: Switch on
cap: Robot on a box: its wheels off the table
Batteries plugged in, switch ON
The switch and the motor driver light up
say: Stand the robot on a box, with its wheels off the table. Plug in the batteries, and switch on. The switch lights up, and so does the motor driver's light.

part: Part 9 · Test it now, while you can reach everything
title: Is it talking?
cap: No answer? Check the 3 wires to the Pi
say: In the LittleBot folder, run: python three, scripts, slash, base test dot pie, ping. It answers pong. Then run it with battery. It shows the batteries' voltage. If ping gets no answer, check the three wires to the Pi.

part: Part 9 · Test it now, while you can reach everything
title: The wheels
term: Spinning the left wheel slowly for 2 seconds...
Did the left wheel turn the way it turns when the
the left encoder counts up going forwards: good
cap: Each wheel spins slowly for 2 seconds
Answer y or n: it sets the directions and saves them
'didn't count'? Check that encoder's 4 wires
say: Run it with wheels. Each wheel spins slowly for two seconds, and it asks which way it turned. It sets the directions, and saves them. It also checks each encoder. If it says one didn't count, check that encoder's four wires.

part: Part 9 · Test it now, while you can reach everything
title: Calibrate the encoders
term: Mark the left wheel (a bit of tape), then press Enter
Turn the left wheel FORWARDS exactly 5 whole turns...
cap: Tape on each wheel · turn it forwards 5 times by hand · Enter
Then switch OFF and unplug the batteries
say: Last, run it with calibrate. Put a bit of tape on each wheel, turn it forwards exactly five times by hand, and press Enter. It saves the result. Then switch off, and unplug the batteries.

part: Part 10 · The head's cables, then the body
title: Plug in the head's cables now
cap: HDMI: its micro end into the Pi's HDMI 0 (next to its USB-C)
The screen's USB-C cable and the camera's USB: Pi USB ports
Leave them, and the head's tail, standing up: tape their tops
say: Part ten. While you can reach the Pi, plug in the head's cables. The H D M I's micro end goes into the Pi's H D M I zero port, the one next to its U S B C. The screen's U S B cable and the camera's U S B go into the Pi's U S B ports. Leave them standing up, with the head servo's long tail, and tape their tops together.

part: Part 10 · The head's cables, then the body
title: The body's 8 nuts
cap: An M3 nut in each of the 8 slots in the body's tongue
Missing? Body upside down, drop them in, a dab of tape on each
say: The body. Check there's an M three nut in each of the eight slots around its bottom edge. If any are missing, turn the body upside down, drop them in, and put a dab of tape over each.

part: Part 10 · The head's cables, then the body
title: Hold the body over the tub, plug in
cap: The slider in through the back, fork first
Speaker + ReSpeaker → the Pi's 2 free USB ports
Each arm servo's plug onto its tail
say: Push the U P S switch slider in through the back, fork first. Hold the body over the tub, or prop it on something. Plug the speaker and the ReSpeaker into the Pi's two free U S B ports. Then push each arm servo's plug onto its tail.

part: Part 10 · The head's cables, then the body
title: A servo's plug onto its tail
cap: brown to brown · red to red · orange to orange
Left arm → the left arm's tail · right → right
A turn of tape around each joint
say: Each jumper's pin goes into the matching hole of the servo's plug. Brown to brown, red to red, and orange to orange. The left arm's servo onto the left arm's tail, and the right onto the right. A servo plugged in backwards won't move. Wrap a turn of tape around each joint.

part: Part 10 · The head's cables, then the body
title: Lower the body, 8 screws
cap: The cables standing up go through its top
Tongue inside the rim · the slider's fork over the UPS switch
8 × M3 × 10 through the rim into the nuts
say: Lower the body. The cables standing up go up through its top. Its bottom edge goes inside the tub's rim, and the slider's fork goes over the U P S switch's knob. Then eight M three by ten, through the rim, into the nuts.

title: Hold the cap over the body
cap: The head servo's plug onto the HEAD tail
The HDMI, USB-C and camera cables up through the neck
Don't lower it yet
say: Part eleven. Hold the cap just over the body's top. Push the head servo's plug onto the head tail, brown to brown. Feed the H D M I, the U S B C and the camera cables up through the neck. Don't lower it yet.

title: Centre the servos, check the head
term: OK - the 3 servos are at 90 degrees and stay there
cap: Batteries in, switch ON, then: center
Sit the head on the neck, facing front: do its 3 holes line up?
No? Loosen the frame's 2 collar screws, re-mesh, tighten
say: Plug in the batteries, switch on, and run center. All three servos go to ninety degrees, and stay there. Now sit the head on the black neck, facing the robot's front, and check its three holes line up with the neck's. If they don't, loosen the servo frame's two collar screws, drop it off the ring gear, turn the neck until they line up, and push it back up. Then switch off.

title: Lower the cap, 8 screws
cap: 8 × M3 × 12 straight down into the collar
Stop when each is snug: they cut their own thread
say: Lower the cap in, and fit eight M three by twelve, straight down into the collar. Stop when each one is snug. They thread into plastic, and too much force strips them.

title: The head
cap: Its cables first: HDMI, the screen's USB-C, the camera
Then onto the black neck, facing front
3 × M3 × 20 down through its floor into the hub's nuts
say: The head. Plug its cables in first: the H D M I, the screen's U S B C, and the camera. Then set it on the black neck, facing front, and fit three M three by twenty, down through its floor, into the nuts in the hub.

title: The arms
cap: The servos are still centred: don't turn them
Each arm onto its spline, hanging down at its side
Then the spline screw
say: The arms. The servos are still centred, so don't turn them by hand. Push each arm onto its servo's spline, hanging down at the robot's side, and fit the spline screw.

title: The drawer goes in last
cap: Plug the drawer into the plug in the bay
Slide it in: the wires fold in above the holder
2 × M3 × 10 through the door
say: Part twelve, the batteries, last. Switch off. Push the drawer's plug into the plug in the bay. Slide the drawer in: the plug and its wires fold into the space above the holder. Then two M three by ten through the door. To change the batteries: switch off, take out the two screws, slide the drawer out, and unplug it.

title: Done
cap: The front switch: wheels and servos · the back slider: the Pi
If something doesn't answer: check that wire's two ends
Unsure? Send a photo
say: That's it. The switch at the front powers the wheels and the servos. The slider at the back turns the Pi on and off. If something doesn't answer, check that wire's two ends against this video. And if you're unsure about anything, send me a photo.
